body:
# Independent audit: log-epsilon selection and unscaled contact compactness

Audited source: `candidate b4f092ee1bb5a205`, with priority on Sections 3--4.



## 1. The source-value tail

The rows are actual probabilities and their original-volume mixture is dm/M, so sigma is a probability. Put q=Delta/epsilon>=a_*>0. The same-force relation and E_i/M<=1 imply

    sigma_i<=kappa_i L_i^(1/N)/a_*.

For 0<l<=1, the exact maximum of l^(1/N)(-log l) is N/e. Summing gives the claimed bound B_*=K_*N/(e a_*) on the sigma-weighted negative logarithms. Since sum sigma_i log L_i=-K_V<=0, the positive logarithms have no larger sum. Markov's inequality therefore gives sigma{L_i>T}<=B_*/log T for T>1. No estimate involving the number of source occurrences is used.

## 2. Passing the tail to actual volume and bounding the maximum

If L_i<=T, the one-sided row comparison L/L_i<=A holds rho_i-almost everywhere and hence also bar_rho_i-almost everywhere. That row puts no original mass on {L>AT}. The exact original-volume mixture proves

    m{L>AT}/M<=sum_(L_i>T) sigma_i.

The direction of the density comparison is correct. Neither a reverse likelihood bound nor a barycenter for bar_rho_i is needed.

For a maximizing point x_0 in a sampled fiber, nonnegative concavity gives L>=L_max/2 on its half-homothetic copy (x_0+K_z)/2. This is an actual subset of that fiber with volume at least 2^(-d)v. If a supremum rather than a maximum is used, the same conclusion follows by approximating it and taking the limit. Taking 1<T<L_max/(2A) puts that whole subset in the STRICT tail {L>AT}. Letting T increase proves

    log(L_max/(2A))<=2^d M B_*/v.

The case L_max<=2A is already covered by the final bound. The printed constant L_* is therefore valid. It is at least one: logarithmic normalization forces L_max>=1, while the probability likelihood comparison itself forces A>=1. This matters for the monotonicity of the power estimates in Section 4.

## 3. Source and inner-core lower bounds

A source inball and the global continuous-coordinate bound give the exact ray estimate

    L_i>=theta max_(K_pi) L,
    theta=r/(r+2R).

Hence log L<=log(L_i/theta) on that WHOLE own fiber. On the other fibers log L<=log L_*. Logarithmic normalization then gives

    0<=V_pi log(L_i/theta)+(M-V_pi)log L_*.

Rearranging proves the source lower bound with the stated sign. Replacing (M-V_pi)/V_pi by the larger M_max/v only weakens it because L_*>=1. The same normalization argument first bounds every fiber maximum below; applying the ray estimate at any point in a fixed inner core gives a uniform lower bound there as claimed. This does not establish a positive uniform boundary floor.

The contained source ball gives E_i>=omega_d r^d, while E_i<=M. Thus f_i=(L_i E_i/M)^(1/N) has fixed positive lower and upper bounds.

For weight comparability, an upper bound on q=Delta/epsilon is automatic from the displayed hypotheses. Summing the same-force relation over the probability sigma gives

    q=sum_i kappa_i f_i<=K_* L_*^(1/N).

Alternatively the earlier exact entropy identity gives the sharper q<=K_*. Together with q>=a_* and f_min<=f_i<=f_max, this proves

    f_min/(K_* f_max) <=sigma_i/kappa_i<=f_max/a_*

for every positive occurrence. Zero occurrences vanish in both arrays. There is no hidden singleton-contact or finite-source-count assumption.

## 4. Conditional scalar selection

Assuming the two-sided value gap and the stated lower semicontinuity/attainment, the scale argument in Section 1 is correct. The endpoint epsilon_bar is excluded for small tau by its fixed positive gap; the test epsilon=tau/C gives the displayed objective upper bound. Writing epsilon_tau=tau s yields the compact sublevel c s-log s<=1+log C and therefore epsilon_tau comparable to tau. This uses no derivative of the optimized value.

Section 2 correctly keeps its additional SAME scalar/body/parameter separator premise. Under that premise its scalar coefficient must balance the penalty and give Delta=tau M. This audit does not replace the missing construction of that separator or assert it from value minimization alone.

The resulting compactness is sampled interior compactness with positive inner-core bounds. Boundary behavior, actual row limits, and any later physical response still require their own arguments.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
